gates.protects: Optional collaboration cannot break AI work, cross accounts, fabricate delivery, lose cached history, or expose unverified decrypted files.
gates.baseline: AI workbench behavior remains unchanged when collaboration is disabled or unavailable; collaboration uses its own encrypted store.
gates.failureFallback: Disable the optional service on initialization failure, retain original durable command identities on ambiguous delivery, fence stopped instances, and reject unauthorized or corrupted data.

gates.protects: Local task classification and verification cannot be disabled by remote configuration.
gates.baseline: The bundled deterministic task registry remains active.
gates.failureFallback: Ignore malformed, disabled, or unsupported remote overlays and use the local baseline.

gates.protects: Retry, rescue, evidence, and TaskRun code agree about side effects and replay safety.
gates.baseline: Unknown tools and shell commands are never replayed automatically.
gates.failureFallback: Treat unknown semantics as external-side-effectful and not replay-safe.

gates.protects: Durable user intent is resolved before capability preparation and dispatch.
gates.baseline: Current-turn deterministic classification uses the original selected model, tools, context, and user text.
gates.failureFallback: Planner or continuity errors return the current-turn baseline without blocking dispatch.

gates.protects: Main, persistence, and renderer share versioned RuntimeEvent and TaskRun contracts.
gates.baseline: Existing event names and TaskRun fields stay compatible.
gates.failureFallback: Reject unsupported versions and malformed typed producer payloads before persistence or rendering.

gates.protects: Workspace version protection remains available to ordinary customers without a manual Git installation and does not regress on large Git-backed workspaces.
gates.baseline: Missing Git or a failed dependency install falls back to the existing local snapshot backend without deleting user files.
gates.failureFallback: Resolve the hidden Git runtime pack first, then system Git; if both are unavailable, keep the local snapshot path and surface the existing coded save error for files beyond its documented bounds.

gates.protects: Internal prompt layers cannot crowd out the original user request.
gates.baseline: Normal-size prompt layers and the full visible user message remain byte-identical.
gates.failureFallback: Bound only oversized internal layers and preserve explicit truncation diagnostics.

gates.protects: External factual claims in known or previously unseen domains cannot be asserted from model memory alone, and the evidence gate cannot make the platform dumber by erasing supported content.
gates.baseline: External fact requests are risk-tiered (hard / verify_soft / advisory) and model-first: only high-stakes asks (the medical/legal/finance floor, or the turn judge's stakes=high verdict) fail closed; ordinary asks auto-verify once and on final failure keep a BOUNDED answer (supported subset or original under a verification banner) — delivered content never drops to zero while any supported content exists. Semantic judgments (support, authority, conflicts, informal labels) belong to one unified judge call per turn, never to domain regex vocabularies; the deterministic layer keeps the literal floor (URL/entity/number grounding, ledger counts) and fabricated entities are never banner-kept. Protection vocabulary covers zh/en/ar equally.
gates.failureFallback: LILY_EVIDENCE_RISK_TIERS=0 restores exact legacy all-hard behavior. Internal gate errors fail closed only on the hard tier; verify_soft/advisory fail open with the original answer. Malformed semantic plans or recovery context preserve the existing strict host gate. A single changed-strategy retry may inherit only bounded successful read-only external evidence from the immediately completed turn; internal retry prompts stay hidden and durable supersession prevents pre-gate engine text from returning on history reload. Otherwise disclose the limit without fabricating an answer.

gates.protects: Image and document reading requests cannot be routed as generation or answered without readable source content.
gates.baseline: The platform resolves operation, source kind, and expected output before routing, then records source coverage separately from tool activity.
gates.failureFallback: Preserve the original attachment and strong model path, disclose the read failure, and replace unsupported source claims before projection.

gates.protects: User edits to a generated or attached file cannot be overwritten from stale attachment snapshots, knowledge-index excerpts, or historical write/edit tool inputs.
gates.baseline: The readable live filesystem path is authoritative; unchanged history remains available and missing live files retain their recoverable historical content.
gates.failureFallback: Use the staged copy only when the original is unavailable, drop fingerprint-mismatched index hits, and require a successful live read before modifying an existing changed file.

gates.protects: Delivered output is not presented as verified completion without required evidence.
gates.baseline: Legacy status remains compatible while completionStatus records verification truth.
gates.failureFallback: Use delivered_unverified or observed_work instead of verified_complete.

gates.protects: A persisted empty assistant turn cannot poison every later model call and prevent tools or compaction from running.
gates.baseline: Healthy text history and tool-call/result protocol messages remain byte-identical and in their original order.
gates.failureFallback: Add one bounded neutral text marker only to truly provider-empty assistant messages; plugin errors and the kill switch retain baseline behavior.

gates.protects: Generated or edited Office and PDF files cannot be presented as polished verified deliverables without an actual output, deterministic structure checks, rendering, and visual inspection.
gates.baseline: Bundled Python authoring remains available for Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and PDF, with managed LibreOffice rendering and CJK-safe font discovery.
gates.failureFallback: Preserve the generated file and label it delivered_unverified; run at most one path-scoped QA continuation, then disclose any remaining verification gap without replaying the authoring task.

gates.protects: Critical modules do not grow new mixed responsibilities or cross process boundaries.
gates.baseline: Existing hotspots may be split and reduced but not enlarged.
gates.failureFallback: The architecture test fails before a capability change can merge.

gates.protects: A user's first upward wheel or touch gesture cannot be overwritten by queued live-render auto-follow callbacks.
gates.baseline: The active conversation follows new output while the user remains at the latest message, and explicit Latest navigation re-enables following.
gates.failureFallback: Cancel stale scheduled auto-follow after any newer navigation intent, preserve the user's reading position, and keep explicit force-to-latest available.

gates.protects: Character card parsing, session binding, or context compilation changes a native turn, crosses conversations, displaces Lily guidance, exposes private card data, or lets imported executable behavior run.
gates.baseline: Native conversations send byte-equivalent Lily/OpenCode prompt bodies with no card parsing or extra model request; character bindings are local, optional, immutable-revision pinned, conversation-scoped, owner-scoped, and snapshotted in the admission transaction; character context is a bounded lower-authority system suffix after the protected Lily prefix.
gates.failureFallback: Disabled, missing, corrupt, oversized, or hostile cards, bindings, revisions, macros, compilation, budgets, and providers without safe system context fail open to the byte-identical native turn with exactly one dispatch; a missing, corrupt, resolver-failing, or over-budget world book never breaks a bound character turn — the character compiles to the byte-identical no-book body (§16) and read-only book inspection stays available; a missing, corrupt, or over-budget persona revision never breaks a bound character turn either — the character+book compiles to the byte-identical no-persona body; authoring edits create new immutable revisions and never alter an already-admitted turn's pinned snapshot or compiled body (update-available requires an explicit apply); retries, recovery, queue promotion, and steer inherit by trusted source turn id instead of rereading the binding; the LILY_CHARACTER_WORLDS=0 kill switch and signed rollout policy restore native behavior without touching stored data; imported scripts, plugins, regex scripts, and unknown macros never execute; an agent draft (tool disabled, kill switch, hostile or over-cap draft input, missing authoring service, malformed injected context block) fails closed to a coded error with NO durable write and the native turn stays byte-equivalent; a workspace pack import with a missing referenced revision or hostile character-worlds section degrades to a native conversation + diagnostic and never leaves a half-imported library (entities import only through validated writers with canonical-hash dedup; bindings restore only when their referenced revisions imported).

gates.protects: A selected character must reach the final model request as an active conversational identity without changing Lily's tools, permissions, safety, evidence, task rigor, exact technical content, or requested output format.
gates.baseline: Native conversations remain byte-identical; selected roles use a host-owned fingerprint-bound activation layer after the protected Lily kernel and a separately delimited lower-authority narrative envelope.
gates.failureFallback: Invalid, unsupported, compile-failed, or over-budget role layers run native Lily and emit metadata-only bypass evidence; only a final-boundary applied receipt scoped to the current session, turn, and immutable revision may render as active.

gates.protects: Character preview actions remain clickable and recover visibly when activation or exit fails.
gates.baseline: The preview banner stays above the active conversation hit-testing layer and reserves message space.
gates.failureFallback: Keep the current preview active, clear busy state, refresh preview state, and show a retryable error instead of leaving a dead control.

gates.protects: AI character, persona, and world-book creation cannot report ordinary files as persisted library entities or trust editable official tags.
gates.baseline: Non-authoring requests retain native Lily behavior; authoring succeeds only after validated immutable library persistence.
gates.failureFallback: Retry failed persistence twice, then explicitly report not saved; preserve the requirement through durable queues and never bind automatically.

gates.protects: A shared engine or broker cannot borrow another conversation's identity, capabilities, workspace, or authority.
gates.baseline: Each broker call is authorized from a signed, expiring, request-scoped host identity.
gates.failureFallback: Reject missing or invalid grants without weakening the native non-broker turn path.

gates.protects: Concurrent agents cannot double-claim work, unlock dependencies early, or cross session mailbox boundaries.
gates.baseline: Task graphs use durable revisioned claims, leases, dependency state, and replay-safe retry policy.
gates.failureFallback: Disable task-graph projection and preserve the existing single-agent TaskRun path.

gates.protects: Partial or corrupt checkpoints cannot be restored and irreversible effects cannot be silently replayed.
gates.baseline: Committed checkpoint manifests are integrity-checked, idempotent, scoped, and preserve fork lineage.
gates.failureFallback: Keep the existing OpenCode revert and in-memory diff behavior when unified checkpoints are disabled.

gates.protects: Headless clients cannot depend on renderer internals or an unstable event stream.
gates.baseline: Legacy JSON remains compatible while versioned NDJSON and SDK contracts are additive.
gates.failureFallback: Use the legacy headless JSON path with stable non-zero exit codes.

gates.protects: Public hooks cannot recurse, leak secrets, hang turns, or mutate protected identity and authority.
gates.baseline: Hooks are schema, timeout, recursion, audit, and mutation bounded.
gates.failureFallback: Observation failures fail open, security denials fail closed, and the hook kill switch bypasses hooks.

gates.protects: Auto/manual choices cannot cross conversations, widen custom pools, lose retry identity, conflate providers, bypass the quality floor for vision, or drift between execution, compaction and usage models.
gates.baseline: Recommended Auto preserves the active model when reliable metadata is absent; per-turn execution profiles drive main/helper models and budgets while retaining bulk-input staging and history compaction.
gates.failureFallback: Recommended Auto can use the legacy active engine only when the catalog is unavailable, not when models are revoked. Expired catalogs refresh once. Ambiguous legacy identities and explicit choices never silently change models.

gates.protects: Packaged Lily can discover installed local command-line software without inheriting unrelated host secrets or unsafe search paths.
gates.baseline: Bundled runtimes and verified packs keep priority while existing absolute platform, installer, inherited, and login-shell executable directories remain discoverable.
gates.failureFallback: Ignore failed login-shell discovery and continue with the bounded known system and installer paths.
